sentences.text: The genus name Wannanosaurus translates to 'Wannan lizard', referencing the specific region where the remains were unearthed.
Scientists know this creature from a single partial skeleton containing a fragment of the skull roof, a lower jaw, a femur, a tibia, and several rib pieces.
Its flat skull roof featuring large openings indicates it belonged to the primitive pachycephalosaur group.
Despite having a femur only 8 cm long, the animal reached an estimated total length of 60 cm.
Fused skull bones confirm that this small individual was an adult when it died.
The species Wannanosaurus yansiensis was formally described by Hou Lian-Hai in 1977.
The fossils were discovered within red sandstone sediments of the Xiaoyan Formation in Anhui, China.
Wannanosaurus likely functioned as a herbivore or omnivore, feeding on low-lying plants and possibly insects.
Researchers sometimes placed Wannanosaurus in the now-deprecated family Homalocephalidae, which included pachycephalosaurs without domed skulls.
A cladogram derived from analyses by Butler and colleagues in 2011 illustrates the modern classification of the genus.
This animal lived during the late Cretaceous, approximately 72 to 69 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
Its time range spans the Maastrichtian stage, extending from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
